section_summary: This section documents the diplomatic coordination, policy disagreements, and practical implementation issues surrounding General Douglas MacArthur's directive requiring the Japanese Government and protecting powers (Switzerland and Sweden) to surrender Japanese diplomatic and consular archives and property abroad to the Four Allied Powers. American diplomatic posts worldwide—particularly in Latin America (including Argentina, Mexico, Colombia, Paraguay, Guatemala, Honduras, and Uruguay) and neutral Europe (Spain and Portugal)—report on local conditions, host government sensitivities regarding sovereign custody versus Allied access, and administrative matters such as legation leases, safe openings, and internee maintenance. The file also reflects British reluctance to pressure belligerent host governments that insist on taking custody themselves, French requests to participate as an Allied power, and inquiries into captured Japanese embassy financial archives in Berlin.

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation clarifying the United States policy against being satisfied with mere access to Japanese archives in Argentina and elsewhere.
subfiles.summary: Oscar S. Straus confers with G. R. Ranken of the British Embassy to dispel a misunderstanding arising from a British telegram suggesting the United States would be content with access alone if host governments object to handing over Japanese archives. Straus emphasizes that U.S. policy aims for full turnover of archives and property to the Four Powers following General MacArthur's directives, particularly in Argentina where ambassadors had planned a fait accompli with the Swiss Minister. Ranken agrees to inform the Foreign Office in London to issue clarifying instructions to British representatives abroad.
subfiles.title: Japanese Archives -- Confusion between U K and U S with regard to Department's policy

subfiles.about: British Embassy telegram reporting on State Department instructions regarding MacArthur's forthcoming directive on Japanese archives and property abroad.
subfiles.summary: The British Embassy in Washington reports to the Foreign Office in London on a State Department circular telegram regarding MacArthur's planned directive to order the surrender of Japanese diplomatic property and archives to the Four Powers. The telegram notes that MacArthur reportedly objected to aspects of the suggested procedure and mentions that the State Department hoped belligerent states would surrender archives, but might accept permission to examine them if host states insisted on taking custody.
subfiles.title: Telegram from British Embassy, Washington, to Foreign Office, London, regarding Japanese Archives Directive

subfiles.about: Letter clarifying the legal distinction between sovereign host-nation action prior to MacArthur's orders and Allied rights after Japanese instructions are issued.
subfiles.summary: Albert E. Clattenburg, Jr. writes to G. R. Ranken to refine the interpretation of their earlier discussions regarding the surrender of Japanese archives. Clattenburg explains that while a host power might exercise sovereign authority to demand custody prior to MacArthur's orders, once Japanese instructions are transmitted to the protecting power without terminating representation, the host government's claim to custody is legally weak. He urges that in Argentina the Allies should avoid inviting government intervention and instead take over archives promptly from the Swiss once Bern transmits instructions.
subfiles.title: Letter to G. R. Ranken regarding Policy on Japanese Diplomatic Property and Archives

subfiles.about: Instruction to the American Embassy in Quito regarding satisfaction with access to Japanese archives and the opening of a safe.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Byrnes informs the Embassy in Quito that because Japanese archives and property have already been turned over and free access permitted, the Department is satisfied with access. The Embassy is authorized to suggest to local authorities that an endeavor be made to open a safe using the best available assistance if it appears to contain documents.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 630 to American Embassy, Quito, regarding Japanese Archives and Safe

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting Allied consensus in Mexico City that the Mexican Government will insist on retaining custody of Japanese archives rather than surrendering them to the Four Powers.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Messersmith acknowledges the Department's circular of October 13 concerning MacArthur's instructions on Japanese archives and reports that his British, Soviet, and Chinese colleagues agree the Mexican Government will refuse to permit the Swedish Legation to deliver archives directly to the Four Powers. As a belligerent nation, Mexico will insist on taking sovereign custody and granting access, identical to the procedure followed for German archives. Messersmith strongly recommends that the Department authorize this procedure for Mexico and other American republics to avoid unnecessary friction over archives that likely contain no significant documents.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 26,916 from Mexico, D. F., regarding Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Archives

subfiles.about: Despatch pointing out the absence of Japanese archives in Guatemala and suggesting the withholding of relevant circular telegrams.
subfiles.summary: First Secretary Robert F. Woodward refers to the Department's circular telegram of October 13 regarding Japanese archives and recalls earlier reports confirming that no Japanese diplomatic mission or archives ever existed in Guatemala. He suggests that the Department could economize by withholding future circular telegrams on this subject from the Embassy in Guatemala.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 735 from Guatemala regarding Economy in Withholding Circular Telegrams

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum transmitting Ranken's letter of October 30 setting forth British policy on Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: J. H. Hibbard forwards G. R. Ranken's letter of October 30 to Philip F. Cherp and suggests conferring after Cherp has reviewed it. Hibbard notes that Ranken inquired whether the Department possessed information on local posts that had not yet approached host governments pursuant to the circular of August 14, specifically asking whether Buenos Aires stood alone in this regard.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum regarding British Embassy Communication on Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Diplomatic letter conveying British instructions that representatives should not press beyond access if a belligerent government objects to surrendering Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: G. R. Ranken replies to Clattenburg's letter of October 15, conveying the views of the British Foreign Office regarding Japanese archives in belligerent countries. While His Majesty's Government supports the Four-Power turnover principle, it considers remaining Japanese archives insufficiently important to justify applying pressure to any belligerent state that objects. Consequently, British representatives have been instructed not to press beyond requesting permission to examine archives if an objection to transfer is raised, acknowledging a formal difference of view with the United States.
subfiles.title: Letter from G. R. Ranken to Albert E. Clattenburg, Jr., regarding British Policy on Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting British and American diplomatic concurrence in Brussels that Belgian custody with Allied access is preferable for Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in Brussels reports informal agreement with the British Embassy that greater convenience and security would be achieved if the Swedish Legation turned Japanese archives over to Belgian authorities, with Allied representatives granted access. The Ambassador concurs with this view rather than demanding surrender directly to representatives of the four Allied nations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1297 from Brussels regarding Japanese Archives in Belgium

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording the Department's position declining a French request to participate in taking over Japanese archives and property.
subfiles.summary: Philip F. Cherp records a telephone consultation with Mr. Colquitt of the Division of Near Eastern Affairs regarding a French diplomatic note requesting participation in taking over Japanese archives and property. Cherp referred to earlier policy memoranda and the circular telegram of October 13, advising that France could not be included as doing so would open the door to similar requests from the Netherlands and other nations. Colquitt agreed to draft a negative reply to the French for routing through the Division of Foreign Activity Correlation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Files regarding French Request to Participate in Japanese Archives Takeover

subfiles.about: Request to the War Department regarding the processing and location of captured Japanese Embassy financial records from Berlin.
subfiles.summary: Frederick B. Lyon requests that the Military Intelligence Division determine the present whereabouts and processing status of two cases of Japanese financial records captured in July 1945 at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin by USFET. The documents, originating from Japanese diplomatic missions and the Yokohama Specie Bank through April 1945, relate to accounts in Germany, Spain, Portugal, and the Balkans. The Division of Economic Security Controls seeks access to these materials, which were routed to MIRS Washington via London.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Present Whereabouts and Processing of Japanese Financial Documents from Berlin

subfiles.about: War Department Military Intelligence Division routing slip circulating the State Department inquiry on captured Japanese financial documents.
subfiles.summary: Major Duncan D. MacBryde routes a copy of the State Department's memorandum of October 17 concerning captured Japanese Embassy financial documents to the Foreign Funds Section of the Military Intelligence Division for action and information. The attached certified copy of the memorandum outlines the capture, description, and transmission route of the Berlin embassy and Yokohama Specie Bank ledgers.
subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Division Routing Slip with Copy of Memorandum on Japanese Documents
subfiles.to: Foreign Funds Section, Military Intelligence Division

subfiles.about: Telegram analyzing financial, custodial, and repatriation responsibilities regarding Japanese property and personnel in Spain.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Norman Armour raises critical questions regarding the assumption of responsibility for Japanese archives, property, and personnel in Spain under the circular of October 13. He recommends leaving official leased premises in Swiss hands for liquidation and cautions against assuming responsibility for Japanese personnel until definitive repatriation plans exist, avoiding the difficulties experienced with German repatriation. Armour notes that Japanese officials in Madrid have submitted a monthly expense budget of 125,000 yen to the Swiss, half of which is for salaries, and will soon require external funding.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2169 from Madrid regarding Japanese Archives, Property, and Personnel in Spain

subfiles.about: Circular telegram transmitting the text of General MacArthur's directive to the Japanese Government regarding diplomatic missions and archives abroad.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Byrnes transmits the text of the directive to be issued by General MacArthur to the Japanese Government at noon on October 25, 1945. The directive orders the Japanese Government to instruct protecting powers (Sweden and Switzerland) to transfer custody of all Japanese diplomatic and consular archives and property to representatives of the Four Allied Powers, except in specified Allied nations where custody is surrendered to the territorial government. In neutral countries, Japanese missions are ordered to surrender property and archives directly to the Four Powers, routine protection of nationals is transferred to Sweden or Switzerland, and Japanese diplomatic personnel are recalled.
subfiles.title: Circular Telegram to All American Diplomatic Missions regarding MacArthur's Directive

subfiles.about: State Department internal memorandum requesting declassification of historical documents for inclusion in the Whiteman Digest of International Law.
subfiles.summary: David Peterson of the Office of the Legal Adviser requests that Ely Maurer review and declassify attached historical State Department papers pursuant to the Foreign Affairs Manual. The declassification is requested so that excerpts and citations may be incorporated into the Whiteman Digest of International Law.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Requesting Declassification of Papers for Whiteman Digest of International Law

subfiles.about: Instruction to the Legation at Tangier to repeat its telegram concerning Japanese archives in Morocco to the Embassy in Madrid.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Byrnes instructs the American Legation at Tangier to repeat its telegram no. 314 of October 24 regarding Japanese archives to the American Embassy in Madrid, if it has not already done so.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Legation, Tangier, Requesting Repetition of Telegram to Madrid

subfiles.about: Letter protesting the Department's circular on Japanese archives and urging acceptance of Mexican sovereign custody with Allied access.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Messersmith writes to John Willard Carrigan criticizing the circular telegram of October 23, arguing that it ignores field recommendations and will provoke diplomatic friction with Mexico and other Latin American republics. Messersmith explains that the Mexican Government and other Allied American republics will never permit foreign powers to assume physical custody of archives on their sovereign soil, though they will readily grant access. Enclosing a paraphrase of the circular telegram, he implores the Department to authorize Chiefs of Mission to agree to host-government custody coupled with Four-Power access.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. Messersmith to John Willard Carrigan with Enclosed Telegram Paraphrase

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting on the location of Japanese consular archives in Casablanca and military attaché records in Madrid.
subfiles.summary: Diplomatic Agent and Consul General Paul H. Alling reports that the only Japanese archives in French Morocco are those of the former Japanese Consulate in Casablanca, currently held along with furniture by the Spanish Consul. He notes that the records of the former Japanese Military Attaché in Tangier were transferred to Madrid when that office closed in May 1944. The Legation is unaware of any Japanese archives or official property in Tangier or Spanish Morocco.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 314 from Tangier regarding Japanese Archives in Morocco

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the absence of Japanese archives in Paraguay and transmitting an explanatory memorandum from the Paraguayan Foreign Ministry.
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy at Asunción reports that inquiries with the Spanish Chargé d'Affaires and the Paraguayan Ministry of Foreign Relations confirm that no Japanese archives exist in Paraguay. The Spanish Chargé stated that all Japanese correspondence was burned before diplomatic personnel departed in 1942, leaving only a couple of flags. An enclosed memorandum from Under Secretary Bruno Alfonso Campos confirms that Commercial Attaché Tomiya Koseki closed the Legation and left for Buenos Aires in early 1942 without leaving any archives or documents.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1220 from Asunción regarding Japanese Archives in Paraguay

subfiles.about: Telegram warning that Tokyo press leaks announcing MacArthur's directive may provoke Argentine interference with the delivery of archives.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires John M. Cabot reports that evening newspapers in Buenos Aires published United Press dispatches from Tokyo announcing that General MacArthur has ordered Japan to surrender all diplomatic archives. Cabot warns that if Argentine authorities impede the delivery of Japanese property and archives under the Department's instructions, this grave indiscretion and premature publicity will be responsible.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2659 from Buenos Aires regarding Press Announcement of Archives Directive

subfiles.about: Circular telegram transmitting the State Department's reply to MacArthur regarding local Four-Power coordination and access negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Byrnes transmits the Department's reply to General MacArthur sent through the Joint Chiefs of Staff concerning coordination among Four-Power representatives and access for other nations at war with Japan. The Department maintains that the reception of archives and property is to be decided in the field by local consultation among the principal diplomatic representatives of the Four Powers present, without the U.S. representative necessarily acting on behalf of all four. Access to archives in countries where the host government takes custody will likewise be negotiated locally by Four-Power representatives.
subfiles.title: Circular Telegram to Diplomatic Missions regarding Coordination and Access Procedures

subfiles.about: Telegram providing instructions on offering Argentina access to archives, Swiss routine functions, office leases, and expense sharing.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Byrnes authorizes the Embassy in Buenos Aires to offer Argentine authorities access to Japanese archives in its notification note, provided the British Embassy concurs. The telegram directs that the Swiss should continue routine protective functions and internee support using Japanese funds, though payments to internees should be reduced. The Department authorizes office rental expenditures if Japanese funds are unavailable, urges sharing storage rental costs with the British, and advises holding property disposal in abeyance.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1563 to Buenos Aires regarding Archives, Swiss Functions, and Leases

subfiles.about: Airgram confirming the absence of Japanese archives in Honduras and requesting exclusion from future circular telegrams.
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy at Tegucigalpa acknowledges the circular of October 23 and reiterates that no Japanese archives exist in Honduras, as papers of the former honorary consul were dispatched to Washington in August 1945. In the interest of economy and efficiency, the Embassy requests that future circular telegrams on the subject not be sent to Honduras, noting that an airgram summary would suffice for records.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-272 from Tegucigalpa regarding Japanese Archives in Honduras

subfiles.about: Telegram requesting authority to offer the Argentine Government access to Japanese archives when notifying them of the takeover.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires John M. Cabot requests authority to include an offer of access in the note informing the Argentine Government that Allied representatives have taken over Japanese archives and property. Cabot notes that former Ambassador Braden previously agreed with British colleagues on the advisability of this step. Informal arrangements are underway for the Swiss Legation to surrender the archives immediately upon receiving instructions from Bern.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2651 from Buenos Aires Requesting Authority to Offer Access to Argentina

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Swiss readiness to surrender archives and detailing questions on internee allowances, office leases, and Japanese staff.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires Cabot reports that the Swiss Legation has agreed informally to deliver Japanese property and archives to American and British custody immediately upon receiving instructions. He requests a definition of routine functions, highlighting that the Swiss currently disburse 15,000 Argentine pesos monthly to interned Japanese diplomats, which will require new financial arrangements if Japanese funds are relinquished. Cabot reports that the lease on the Japanese residence was terminated, recommends terminating the Belgrano office lease in favor of downtown rooms, and requests guidance on the internment of Chancellor Tani and surplus property disposal.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2658 from Buenos Aires regarding Swiss Custody, Leases, and Internee Support

subfiles.about: Telegram informing the Embassy in Lisbon that implementation of MacArthur's directive by Tokyo has not yet been confirmed.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Byrnes informs the American Embassy in Lisbon, in reference to its telegram no. 2165 of October 26, that the Department has not yet been informed whether the Japanese Government has implemented the directive issued by General MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Embassy, Lisbon, regarding Implementation of MacArthur's Directive

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting consultations among Allied envoys in Bogota regarding Japanese archives, joint sealing, and legation lease expenses.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador John C. Wiley reports conferring with his British and Soviet colleagues regarding the October 23 circular on Japanese archives in Colombia. Wiley dissuaded the Soviet Minister from insisting on turning archives over to the Colombian Foreign Office and suggested British custody as senior envoy, leading to a plan to jointly inspect and seal the archives once surrendered by the Swiss Chargé. Owing to the large volume of archives, they recommend maintaining the Japanese Legation lease using frozen Japanese funds held by Colombia (approximately 90,000 pesos), pending further instructions from Moscow and Washington.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1321 from Bogota regarding Allied Consultations on Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Telegram inquiring whether the Japanese Government has sent instructions to its Lisbon representative under MacArthur's directive.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Herman B. Baruch reports that an Embassy representative met with British and Chinese colleagues to formulate plans regarding Japanese interests in Portugal. To facilitate their coordinated action, Baruch asks the Department to confirm whether the Japanese Government has transmitted instructions to its representative in Lisbon as required under paragraphs 1-C and 1-D of General MacArthur's directive.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2165 from Lisbon Inquiring on Japanese Government Compliance

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation discussing press announcements of MacArthur's directive with the Chilean Chargé d'Affaires.
subfiles.summary: Joseph F. Flack confers with Chilean Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Arturo Bascuñán regarding press reports of General MacArthur's directive on Japanese archives abroad. After consulting Philip F. Cherp, Flack explains that Allied representatives will form committees to receive archives and property from protecting powers, while routine protection of nationals will continue under Switzerland or Sweden. Flack notes that because the Soviet Union lacks representation in Santiago, the three powers present will consult, and archives will likely remain in their existing building.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Arturo Bascuñán regarding MacArthur's Directive

subfiles.about: Airgram reporting bank balances held in the name of the Japanese Legation in Montevideo.
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy at Montevideo refers to the circular telegram of October 23 and reports that while no Japanese archives exist in Uruguay, bank accounts in the name of the Japanese Legation are held at the Banco de la República. The account, titled "Cuenta Corriente Legación del Japón", contains 205,888.85 Uruguayan pesos. The Embassy notes that no immediate action is required pending further instructions.
subfiles.title: Airgram from Montevideo regarding Japanese Legation Accounts in Uruguay
